reason: Verified by driving master.html?state=day at 390x844 and 1440x960 and opening .b-behindDetails (open=false at rest, so both gates and every shot miss it). Measured tops inside .b-measure.b-back, identical at both widths: numerals .b-away at 30/58/72/86/114/128/338/550; titles at 28/77/126/175/224/273/336/548; --push on .b-copy 0/21/56/91/112/147/0/0. So 14 pairs, 168 and 274 pair, and the middle six break: '35' (72) is 5px from 'Final guest numbers' (77) and 54px from its own 'Choose the evening music'; '63' (128) sits beside 'Choose the evening music' (126); 'Final dress fitting', 'Send the invitations' and 'Menu tasting at The Orchard' have no numeral within 47px. Five of eight rows carry a figure belonging to another moment or none - the seat's count is exact. The cause is in place() (render-b.js ~line 270): only .b-copy gets --push, per the stated rule in b.css ('The tick and the count sit on the true pixel, always. Only the words are pushed clear'). That rule is sound on the forward rail and was designed for it - at 14px/day the shipped fixture never crowds at all (data-crowded is 'false' on every item in phone/desk/owner-flight/print), so push is a rare, small, owner-induced nudge there. At BACK_PX=2 it is not rare: it fires structurally and permanently on six of eight rows of the one surface the company is judged by. The gates cannot see it and do not restate it: collisions() explicitly measures only .b-copy rects and encodes the same assumption in its own comment; the day-state assertion checks only px, row count and rail presence; the stacked-day assertion covers same-day coincidence, which is a different case handled by data-stack='follow'. The screen-reader path is fine (.b-unitSaid speaks 'N days back' inside each row), which makes this a sighted-only failure - the accessible name is right and the picture is wrong. Not taste: the numerals are per-row labels of arbitrary values, not regular graduations of a scale, so their position carries no information the written figure does not already carry; the tick is what encodes position, and it can stay. The forward rail sets the promise that count and title are level, and the past rail silently breaks it. Fix is polish-sized (one CSS custom property applied to one more element, plus a connector), touches no colour, weight or architecture, and leaves the 'position is the quantity' assertion passing because .b-item style.top is unchanged.
sharpenedFix: In place(), set the same --push on the row element rather than on .b-copy alone, and have .b-away consume it (margin-top: var(--push,0px)) so the figure travels with the words it names; leave .b-tick on the true pixel and leave .b-item[style.top] untouched so 'measure is strictly proportional' and 'both stay on the true pixel' keep passing. Draw the connector as an elbow rather than a diagonal: on [data-crowded='true'] only, a 1px hairline in var(--fore-28) running down the gutter between the count column and the rail from the tick's true pixel to the pushed numeral's mid-height, then 6px horizontally into the numeral - six short diagonals fanning across the count column would be noisier than the problem. aria-hidden on the connector (the row already speaks its unit), and mirror it under forced-colors with CanvasText as .b-tick already is. Keep .b-item[data-stack='follow'] hiding the count so same-day pairs still share one mark and one figure, and keep the [data-crowded='true'] copy halo. Only the day state passes back:true, so the blast radius is one surface; re-run interaction-check.mjs plus a new assertion that on state=day, disclosure open, every .b-back row's .b-away vertical centre is within half a row of its own .b-title's.
